correctness.rationale: Two independent standard-library programs enumerate all 3,683 subsets of size at most three on two explicit Fano-plane Coxeter representations and verify exactly 336 minimum three-sensor power-dominating sets. Both construct 336-state jump/slide graphs, check the 28 six-state matching-supported mobile cycles and 168 isolated states, and compute all 56,280 unordered shortest jump distances. Their exact outputs agree. This establishes a finite exhaustive proof, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: The Coxeter graph is a canonical vertex-transitive cubic girth-seven network, and its exact three-sensor optimum relocation structure is a natural complete benchmark. The sharp contrast between 168 immobile states and 28 geometric six-cycles under physical slides, versus universal connectivity in six jumps, exposes a mathematically specific mobility obstruction. The three-edge matching support and missing opposite corners explain the cycle structure, giving structural content beyond a list of counts; no infinite family is needed for this finite finding.
